record.original_question: Determine whether C9 admits instantaneous uniform mixing for the continuous-time quantum walk.

evidence.quote: This leads us to our next open problem. Like the Hadamard graph, C9 is also a formally self-dual distance-regular graph of diameter 4. Unfortunately, it seems that the application of Corollary 3.3 is much more diffcult in this case.
3.2 Open Problem. Determine if C9 admits uniform mixing.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C_9$ denote the cycle graph on $9$ vertices, with vertex set $\mathbb{Z}/9\mathbb{Z}$ and edges $\{i,i+1\}$ for $i \in \mathbb{Z}/9\mathbb{Z}$. Let $A$ be its $0/1$ adjacency matrix. The continuous-time quantum walk on $C_9$ is the one-parameter family of unitary operators
$$U(t) = \exp(itA), \qquad t \in \mathbb{R},$$
and the associated mixing matrix at time $t$ is the doubly stochastic matrix
$$M(t) = U(t) \circ \overline{U(t)}, \qquad M(t)_{u,v} = |U(t)_{u,v}|^2,$$
where $\circ$ denotes the entrywise (Hadamard) product. The graph $C_9$ is said to admit instantaneous uniform mixing if there exists a positive real number $\tau$ such that
$$M(\tau) = \tfrac{1}{9}\, J,$$
where $J$ is the $9\times 9$ all-ones matrix; equivalently, $|U(\tau)_{u,v}|^2 = \tfrac{1}{9}$ for every pair of vertices $u,v$.

Question: Does $C_9$ admit instantaneous uniform mixing?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the 9-cycle $C_9$ admits instantaneous uniform mixing for its continuous-time quantum walk is explicitly listed as an open problem in a 2024 survey on selected open problems in continuous-time quantum walks. Earlier results of Godsil–Mullin–Roy rule out uniform mixing on even cycles and on cycles of prime length, but $C_9$ remains unresolved, and no published resolution was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Determine if C9 admits uniform mixing... Like the Hadamard graph, C9 is also a formally self-dual distance-regular graph of diameter 4.
status_evidence.claim: The status of instantaneous uniform mixing for the 9-cycle C9 is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Non-uniform mixing of quantum walk on cycles
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum walks on cycles fail to achieve uniform mixing in many cases.
status_evidence.claim: Prior results exclude uniform mixing for cycles of even length and prime length, leaving C9 as a notable open case.
